commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot and add greeting flow
Store tasks and list them on request
Model tasks and support completion updates
Add typed tasks and reusable UI tests
Use a dynamic collection and support task deletion
Represent command routing with an enum

commitResults.messageBody:
The repository includes a custom UI-testing skill that the course does
not require. It also duplicates direct verification.

Remove the skill and its project instruction so future increments use
JDK 25 directly.

Tasks disappear whenever Nori exits, preventing users from resuming
their task list in a later session.

Add file-backed storage that creates missing data paths, restores task
types and completion states, and saves after every mutating command.

Persistent storage has been implemented and tested independently on
the feature branch.

Integrate it after verifying file creation, task reload, status changes,
and deletion across separate JDK 25 runs.

Deadline values are stored as text, so invalid calendar values are
accepted and date-time information cannot be handled consistently.

Store deadlines as LocalDate and LocalTime values. Accept ISO and slash
separated date-time input, format it for display, and preserve both
components through persistent storage.

Date and time handling has been implemented and tested independently on
the feature branch.

Integrate it after verifying valid, invalid, and persisted deadlines with
JDK 25.

The custom UI test workflow has already been removed, so its manual test
plan is no longer used and is not required by the course.

Remove the stale plan to keep the repository aligned with the supported
testing workflow.

Nori handles input, parsing, task operations, and persistence
coordination in one class, making each responsibility harder to change
and test independently.

Move user interaction into Ui, command interpretation into Parser, and
task collection operations into TaskList. Keep Nori as the application
coordinator and adapt Storage to use the task-list abstraction.

The Java classes use the unnamed package, which obscures component
boundaries and does not match the conventional source layout expected
by later build tools.

Place the application in the nori package and group parsing, storage,
task, and UI classes into cohesive subpackages. Keep src/main/java as
the source root.
